round_about: A study of one bare tree in winter, grown with the engine's tree-growth model.
title: Old Oak in Snow (a study)
title_source: r12-tree3:notes/r12_tree3.md:1 (program header r12-tree3:paintings/src/bin/r12_tree3.rs:1 has 'Old Oak in Snow, a study')
subject: One ancient oak, its top dead and broken into silver-gray wood, stands alone on a low rise of snow under a still, clouded late-afternoon sky with a pale glow low on the left.
final_note: the painter's 2400 px render; pixel-identical to the copy in notes/round12/look
painter_words: The dead grey against the live near-black gives the tree a story. The sky's warm low band behind the bole puts the darkest dark against the lightest light, where the eye should go. In short, a believable old oak, painted with a hand, standing in a placeholder landscape.

round_about: The same tree study with the growth model taken away: each painter drew its tree limb by limb.
subject: An old stag-headed oak, two bleached dead limbs standing above its living crown and one limb sawn to a stub, stands alone on a low swell of snow under a cold gray-blue sky, a fallen limb half buried at the right.
final_note: the painter's 2400 px render; pixel-identical to the copy in notes/round13/look
painter_words: The twigs are the best passage: pointed-rigger strokes lifted off to the tip, warm gray-brown against the cold sky, overlapping into a filigree that looks painted, not rendered. Snow on the limbs is thin and timid. Only a few bands show at viewing distance, so the tree barely says "snow has fallen".

round_about: A chain of painters: each paints a landscape of its choosing and leaves craft notes for the next one.
title: Ploughed field before Greifswald, October morning
subject: A ploughed field with crows and a heap of field stones rises to a low crest, and beyond it the towers of a small Baltic town stand in morning mist, with a cart track winding up toward them.
final_note: the painter's 2400 px render; pixel-identical to notes/round14/look/p1a_ploughed_field_2400.png
painter_words: The eye runs up the furrows and the track to the town. The town silhouette (spire, bulbed tower, squat tower, naves) is the one firm, found shape in the picture. Its foot dissolves into mist laid wet over it, which is where I wanted the picture's tension.

reception.quote: I kind of like it
it's not a Friedrich
very funny ... adorable

remarks: Title uses British 'Ploughed' verbatim. Same notes filename as r14-p1 but on branch r14a-p1; the r14-p1 branch has the later painting.

round_about: A chain of painters: each paints a landscape of its choosing and leaves craft notes for the next one.
title: Morning in the Mountains
subject: From a granite summit before sunrise, a small man seen from behind stands on the highest rock facing the glow over mountain ranges that recede through a sea of mist, with spruces on the right and a thin old moon above.
time_note: the final session; a 3-minute false start (22:25 UTC) preceded it
final_note: the painter's 2400 px render; pixel-identical to notes/round14/look/p1_2400.png
painter_words: The small dark figure on the highest rock against the brightest mist is where the eye lands and then goes on to where he looks. Friedrich would have put something there (a path, a plant drawn from a study) that rewards looking close. My attempt at stones failed; I didn't find the thing.

round_about: A chain of painters: each paints a landscape of its choosing and leaves craft notes for the next one.
title: Evening over the flat country
title_source: r14-p2:paintings/src/bin/r14_p2.rs:1 (notes heading r14-p2:notes/r14_p2.md:1 adds '(a distant town after sunset)')
subject: Just after sunset, a small town stands as a silhouette on the far edge of a flat, marshy coastal plain by a lagoon, while two small figures seen from behind watch from a dark rise under a thin crescent moon.
final_note: the painter's 2400 px render; pixel-identical to notes/round14/look/p2_2400.png
painter_words: The young moon with its ashen light, placed off the glow's axis with its lit limb toward the sunken sun, is right and quiet. That emptiness is Friedrich's, but his empty passages are finer and more deliberate than mine.
remarks: The notes heading gives the longer form 'Evening over the flat country (a distant town after sunset)'; the parenthetical reads as a subtitle.

round_about: A chain of painters: each paints a landscape of its choosing and leaves craft notes for the next one.
title: Evening on the Baltic shore
subject: After sunset on a stony Rügen beach, a woman in a dark gown stands at the water's edge between a line of fishermen's stakes and a granite erratic, looking toward the afterglow under a thin young moon.
final_note: the painter's 2400 px render; pixel-identical to notes/round14/look/p3_2400.png
painter_words: The woman is the one hard shape, her head just over the sea's rim, and the eye goes to her and then to the glow. The upper sky is soft and a little heavy; a painter with another day would lay it once more, cleaner, and let the blue sing.

round_about: The chain again from a stripped-down studio with only the tools and notes a painter needs.
title: Evening over a Misty Valley in the Mountains
subject: A few minutes after sunset in late October, a small figure with a staff stands on a dark heath knoll with two tall spruces, looking over a mist-filled valley where four ranges recede toward the afterglow under a thin crescent moon.
final_note: the painter's 2400 px render; pixel-identical to notes/round15/look/p1_2400.png
painter_words: He is small, so the space stays large. He stands where the mist is palest, so a small dark shape carries the most contrast in the picture. That vertical link from man to moon replaces any gesture.

round_about: The chain again from a stripped-down studio with only the tools and notes a painter needs.
title: Oak in the snow at dusk
subject: On a winter evening after sunset, an old stag-headed oak with crows in it stands on a snowy rise at the left, while a lone walker follows a trodden path across the snow plain toward a Gothic church on the horizon under the evening star.
time_note: 235 min in the log minus two hung ImageMagick/Inkscape conversions of an SVG sketch (125 and 60 min tool calls, killed by the integrator; notes/round15/README.md)
final_note: the painter's 2400 px render; pixel-identical to notes/round15/look/p2_2400.png
painter_words: An old dead tree and a living walker are joined by the path to the church under the evening star. I kept it quiet: small figure, no dramatic light. I meant that emptiness; it is right for him, but the picture's weight sits left.

round_about: The chain again from a stripped-down studio with only the tools and notes a painter needs.
title: Morning on the Baltic shore
subject: Before sunrise on a calm Baltic shore, a woman in a dark dress and red shawl stands at the water's edge facing the glow, with net poles on a low dune to the left, a granite boulder on the right and a waning crescent high in the sky.
final_note: the painter's 2400 px render; pixel-identical to notes/round15/look/p3_2400.png
painter_words: It is empty in the way his *Monk* and his shore pictures are: the subject is the light and the waiting. They are the verticals that cross the horizon: human work, idle at this hour.
remarks: First quote keeps the markdown italics around *Monk* (Friedrich's Monk by the Sea). The second quote is about the net poles.
